bill.title: Supporting Apprenticeship Colleges Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

industries.rationale: The bill provides federal grants directly to institutions of higher education that sponsor apprenticeship programs.
The bill specifically targets construction-oriented registered apprenticeship programs and would fund outreach to construction businesses.
The bill specifically targets manufacturing-oriented registered apprenticeship programs and would fund outreach to manufacturing businesses.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would direct the Department of Education to award grants to colleges and universities that run registered apprenticeship programs in construction and manufacturing. The grants would help these institutions expand outreach to high schools and local businesses, and provide advising and support services to students enrolled in the apprenticeship programs.

bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to Public Land Order No. 7917 for Withdrawal of Federal Lands; Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, MN.

industries.rationale: The bill would directly reopen over 225,000 acres to mineral exploration and leasing that are currently withdrawn from such activity.
The bill affects protections for wilderness areas and watersheds, directly implicating environmental and conservation advocacy organizations.
The bill would reopen the lands to geothermal energy leasing and development alongside mineral leasing.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution would reverse a federal order that withdrew approximately 225,504 acres of national forest land in northeastern Minnesota from mineral and geothermal leasing. The original order, issued in 2023, was intended to protect the Rainy River Watershed and the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness from potential mining impacts for 20 years. If passed, the resolution would reopen these lands to mineral exploration and development, as well as geothermal energy leasing.

plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.

bill.title: No Taxpayer Funding for Abortion and Abortion Insurance Full Disclosure Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Ways and Means, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.

industries.rationale: The bill directly restricts what health insurance plans may cover and how federal subsidies interact with abortion coverage in qualified health plans.
The bill prohibits federal health care facilities and federal employees from providing abortion services, affecting facilities that currently receive federal funds.
Organizations focused on reproductive health policy and abortion access or restrictions have a direct stake in the regulatory framework this bill establishes.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would make permanent the restrictions on federal funding for abortion services and health insurance coverage that includes abortion. Currently, these restrictions are renewed each year through appropriations bills; the bill would apply them across all federal programs and funds. It would also prohibit qualified health plans offered through insurance marketplaces from covering abortion. The bill includes exceptions for cases of rape, incest, or when the pregnant person's life is in danger.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys health insurance. Anyone who pays a medical bill.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act
bill.latestActionText: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers working with controlled substances and affects the regulatory classification of fentanyl-related compounds.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect defense attorneys and prosecutors handling drug trafficking cases.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and makes it easier for registered researchers to conduct certain activities without additional permits.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act
bill.latestActionText: Read the second time. Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 10.

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates new litigation exposure for federal agencies, affecting federal and state government operations and budgets.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, increasing demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would require the Department of Homeland Security to detain individuals who are in the country without authorization and have been arrested for or charged with burglary, theft, larceny, or shoplifting. It would also allow state governments to sue the federal government for injunctive relief when federal immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing individuals from custody or not fulfilling visa or asylum processing requirements—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.title: Concerning the National Collegiate Athletic Association policy for eligibility in women's sports.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Education and Workforce.

industries.rationale: The resolution directly addresses NCAA policy, which governs collegiate athletics at member universities and affects their compliance obligations and program administration.
Changes to NCAA eligibility rules could affect the composition and marketability of collegiate sports programming and events.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution calls on the National Collegiate Athletic Association to withdraw its current policy allowing transgender student-athletes to compete and instead adopt rules requiring participation in women's sports to be based on biological sex. The measure urges the NCAA to mandate that all member conferences implement such a policy across every sport and division. As a resolution, it expresses the position of the House but does not create enforceable law.

bill.title: Recognizing Charleston as the appropriate host city for the 2027 annual meeting of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe Parliamentary Assembly.
bill.latestActionText: Referred to the House Committee on Foreign Affairs.

industries.rationale: Hosting a large international parliamentary assembly would generate demand for hotel rooms, event venues, and tourism services in Charleston.

bill.plainSummary: This resolution recognizes Charleston, South Carolina, as the appropriate host city for the 2027 annual meeting of the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe Parliamentary Assembly. It is a ceremonial measure expressing the House's support for Charleston to host this international parliamentary gathering. The resolution does not create legal obligations or change policy.
